units.translation: For a woman leads a man in golden armor, a warrior, to see.
a bright serpent rushing forth from a golden-wrought cord.

Thus from the apograph, instead of χρυσονόμου [of golden pasture], which is in M. The scholiast records both readings, who on χρυσονόμου [of golden pasture] noted: νῦν τῆς πλουσίας · τινὲς γὰρ ἀνέγνωσαν χρυσογόνου διὰ τὸ τὸν Περσέα ἀπὸ χρυσοῦ γεγενῆσθαι · ὁ καὶ βέλτιον [now of the rich one; for some read χρυσογόνου because Perseus was born from gold; which is also better]. And in another scholium: τῆς Περσέως γενεᾶς ἀπόγονος · ἢ τῆς τῶν χρυσῶν ἀνθρώπων · ἢ πολυχρύσου [descendant of the race of Perseus; or of the golden race of men; or rich in gold]. Similarly Soph. Ant. 950 Ζεὺς ταμιεύεσκε (Danaae) γονὰς χρυσορύτους [Zeus dispensed (to Danae) gold-flowing offspring], i.e. Perseus.
a godlike man of the race born of gold.
now of the rich one; for some read χρυσογόνου because Perseus was born from gold; which is also better
descendant of the race of Perseus; or of the golden race of men; or rich in gold
Thus Hermann, instead of χρυσεοδμήτοισιν [built of gold].
Thus Auratus, instead of δ᾽ ἐσθλά [but good things].
Another example of this word is in Eurip. Phoen. 946, who said χρυσοπήληκα στάχυν σπαρτῶν [the golden-helmeted crop of the Sown Men].
the golden-helmeted crop of the Sown Men
χρυσορύτους [gold-flowing] is in Soph. Ant. 950. After Aeschylus and Sophocles only some writers of the lowest age used it, as indicated in the Thesaurus vol. 8 p. 1745.
they dwell around the gold-flowing stream of Pluto's passage.
These things, my child, you say are better than gold.
the gold-shining light, like a sun, sent word to the watch-posts of Macistus.
[On accent and declension see Thes. vol. 8 p. 1761 and 1764. The oblique cases are χρωτός χρωτί χρῶτα and, where the meter requires, χροός χροΐ (or χρῷ) χρόα.] skin, surface of the body.
where it is said of the changed color of skin sprinkled with blood: on which see Thes. vol. 8 p. 1763.

Dative χροΐ [to the skin]. Thus I corrected what is in M: πρὶν ἄνδρ᾽ ἀπευκτὸν τῷδ᾽ ἐχριμφθῆν χροῖν [before a hateful man should touch this skin], from which in the Scorialensian apograph was made τῷδ᾽ ἐγχριμφθῆναι χροΐ [to touch this skin], in others τῷδ᾽ ἐγχριμφθῆναι χεροῖν [to touch with hands], by conjecture of a copyist. To this passage undoubtedly refer the glosses of Hesychius: χρημφθῆναι (thus the codex, and that is required by the order of letters, as χρήμπτει in the preceding gloss): προσελάσαι, ἐγγίσαι, ἐνορμῆσαι [to drive near, to approach, to rush upon]. And below χριμφθῆναι: ἐμπελασθῆναι, ἐκριφῆναι (?), ἀνορμῆσαι [to approach, to be cast out (?), to rush up]. And χροΐ: σώματι, ἐπιφανείᾳ [to the body, to the surface].
